children.translated_text: Even now [I think of] her, fair as a garland of golden <s>campaka</s> blossoms,
with a face like a full-blown lotus, with a delicate line of hair [on her belly],
risen from sleep, her limbs languid and agitated by desire —
I think of [her] like knowledge enhanced by heedlessness.
Even now, her — moon-faced, rich in fresh youth,
with full breasts — if again I were to see [her], of fair and lovely complexion,
her limbs tormented by the fire of <s>Manmatha</s>'s (Love's) arrows —
I would at once make my limbs perfectly cool.
Even now, if I again [see] her, with eyes wide as lotuses,
wearied by the weight of her full breasts —
pressing [her] with both arms, I would drink her face
like a maddened bee [drinking] a lotus at will.

children.text: adya api tāṃ yadi punaḥ kamala-āyata-akṣīṃ

children.translated_text: Even now [I remember] her, her limbs unable to bear the exhaustion of lovemaking,
with locks and tresses fallen upon her pale cheeks,
bearing a slow [gait] caused by secret sin,
with vine-like arms clinging to [my] neck — I remember [her].
Even now [I remember] her, with eyes rolling from the vigil of lovemaking,
the pupils restlessly moving sidewise in her wide eyes,
a royal swan on the lake that is the essence of love (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>),
her face bowed with modesty, at dawn — I remember [her].
Even now, if again [I see] her, with eyes extending to her ears,
[her] slender body feverish from long separation —
embracing her with my limbs exceedingly tightly,

children.text: nonmīlayāmi nayane na ca tāṃ tyajāmi
children.translated_text: I would not open my eyes, nor would I let her go.

children.text: adya api tāṃ yadi punaḥ śravaṇa-āyata-akṣīṃ
na unmīlayāmi nayane na ca tāṃ tyajāmi

children.translated_text: Even now [I remember] her, the stage-director of the dance of lovemaking,
with a face beautiful as the full moon, limbs overwhelmed with passion,
slender, bowed by the weight of her broad hips and breasts,
with an abundance of flowing, disheveled tresses — I remember [her].
Even now [I remember] her on the bed, with the fragrance
of smooth sandalwood paste mixed with musk spreading [from her body],
her eyelashes clinging together from mutual beak-like kissing,
her pair of lovely eyes — I remember [her] on the bed.
Even now [I remember] her in lovemaking, flushed from drinking wine,
with playful lips, slender body, and restless wide eyes,
her body anointed with Kashmiri saffron paste and musk,
her mouth full of camphor and betel — I remember [her].
Even now [I remember] the face of my beloved,
golden-fair with body-unguent, covered with beads of perspiration,
at the end [of love], with eyes rolling from the exhaustion of passion —
like the disk of the moon released from the eclipse of <s>Rāhu</s>.
Even now it revolves in my mind:
when at night I sneezed, the princess
set aside the auspicious word 'Live!' out of anger,
[and instead,] without speaking, placed a golden [ear-]leaf upon my ear.
Even now I remember the face of my beloved in the inverted love-posture,
her cheeks grazed by her golden earrings,
covered with dense, distinct drops of sweat from the exertion of rocking,
scattered like a shower of pearls.
Even now I remember her heavy glances of broken affection,
her graceful poses in the confusion of love,
the lovely end of her breasts slipping from the edge of her garment,
and her lip adorned by teeth-marks.
Even now [I remember] her, her hands red like fresh <s>aśoka</s> shoots,
the tips of her nipples kissed by clusters of pearls,
the surface of her cheeks pale from suppressed laughter —
that beloved one with the gait of a spotless swan — I remember [her].
Even now I remember the mark of nail-scratches
placed upon her dense, golden-hued thighs,
and when she arose, pulling her gleaming golden garment,
clutching it in her hand out of modesty as she departed.
Even now [I remember] her, with rolling eyes adorned with collyrium,
standing on the ground, her mass of hair disordered with abundant flowers,
the beauty of her teeth [glimpsed] amid vermilion and pearls,
wearing golden bangles — I remember [her] in private.
Even now [I remember] her, with her mass of hair loosened from its bonds,
her garlands fallen, her lower lip sweet as the nectar of a smile,
with a beautiful pearl necklace kissing
the surface of her full, high pair of breasts — I remember her with rolling eyes, in private.
Even now I think of her, in the white mansion,
where the darkness was dispelled by the rays of rows of jeweled lamps,
when she had made the effort to come secretly for a face-to-face meeting,
her eyes [expressing] modesty, fear, and entreaty — I think of [her].
Even now [I remember] her, her limbs oppressed by the fire of separation,
slender, deer-eyed, the sole vessel of love,
wearing various and wonderful ornaments —
that beautiful-toothed woman with the gait of a royal swan — I remember [her].
Even now [I remember] her, laughing, bowed by the weight of her breasts,
the region of her throat made white by a pearl necklace —
upon that mountain of pleasure, the beautiful, brilliant banner
of the Flower-armed one (<s>Kāma</s>) — I remember [my] beloved.
Even now I remember the words of my beloved,
overwhelmed by the exhaustion of love —
uttered indistinctly, timidly spoken,
with mingled syllables, beautiful — [conveying] the meaning appropriate to a hundred flatteries and difficult endearments.
Even now I think of her, her eyes closed and rolling in lovemaking,
her slender body limp, garments and tresses slipping away,
a royal swan in the lotus-forest of love —
I think of [her] in another birth also, even in death.
Even now, her — the loving one with eyes of a young deer,
bearing a pair of pitcher-breasts full of ambrosia —
if I were to see her again at the close of day,
I would abandon the pleasures of heaven, liberation, and kingship.
Even now [I remember] my beloved,
foremost in the line of the choicest women on earth by the beauty of all her limbs,
the supreme drinking-vessel of the <s>rasa</s> (essence) of the drama of love,
afflicted by the arrows of the Flower-armed one (<s>Kāma</s>) — I remember [her].
Even now, her body clinging [to mine] like a still garment,
her body heated by the intense fire of mature passion —
the young girl, shelterless, pitiable,

children.text: prāṇādhikāṃ kṣaṇam ahaṃ na hi vismarāmi
children.translated_text: dearer than life — not for a single moment do I forget her.

children.text: adya api tāṃ stimita-vastram iva aṅga-lagnāṃ
prāṇādhikāṃ kṣaṇam ahaṃ na hi vismarāmi

children.translated_text: Even now I think of the princess,
foremost among excellent beauties, fashioned as the sole vessel of love:
'Alas, my people! This fire of separation
cannot be endured!' — thus I think [of her words].
Even now, setting aside [even] the wonder-causing gods,

children.text: buddhir balāc calati me kim ahaṃ karomi
children.translated_text: my mind forcefully turns [to her] — what can I do?
Even knowing that at this time of death, every moment,
[I think:] 'My beloved!' 'My dearest!' 'Mine!' — she who is steadfast.

children.text: buddhir balāc calati me kim ahaṃ karomi
kānta īti vallabhatara īti mama iti dhīrā
adyāpi tāṃ gamanam ity uditaṃ madīyaṃ
children.translated_text: Even now, when she heard that my departure had been announced,
like a timid doe with restless eyes,
her eyes troubled with streaming, flowing tears, her words faltering,
her face bent low with heavy grief — I think of [her].

children.text: adya api tāṃ gamanam ity uditaṃ madīyaṃ

children.translated_text: Even now [I think of] her, whose face
I have never seen equaled, despite my most careful searching,
whose beauty surpasses <s>Rati</s> and the luster of the king of birds,
my beloved, by the great quality of her supreme purity.

children.text: adya api tāṃ sunipuṇaṃ yatatā maya āpi

children.translated_text: Even now I remember her, whose momentary separation is comparable to poison,
whose company is a more-than-ample bath of nectar,
who sustains [my] life, who is a parasol against the sun of love,
with upswept masses of hair — that beautiful-toothed woman — I remember [her].
Even now, when I was being led from the bed-chamber
by irresistible, terrifying men resembling the messengers of <s>Yama</s> —

children.text: kiṃ kiṃ tayā bahuvidhaṃ na kṛtaṃ madarthe
children.translated_text: what, what manifold things did she not do for my sake?

children.text: vaktuṃ na pāryateti vyathate mano me
children.translated_text: 'It cannot be told!' — thus my mind is pained.

children.text: kiṃ kiṃ tayā bahuvidhaṃ na kṛtaṃ mad-arthe
vaktuṃ na pāryata iti vyathate mano me
adyāpi me niśi divā hṛdayaṃ dunoti
children.translated_text: Even now, night and day, my heart is pained
[by the thought of] my beloved's face, beautiful as the full moon,
whose loveliness surpasses <s>Rati</s> and the pride of <s>Kāma</s> —

children.text: bhūyaḥ puraḥ pratipadaṃ na vilokyate yat
children.translated_text: for it is not seen again before me at every step.

children.text: adya api me niśi divā hṛdayaṃ dunoti
bhūyaḥ puraḥ pratipadaṃ na vilokyate yat

children.translated_text: Even now, with steadfast mind,
I think of that young woman, my hope of life,
the essence of fresh youth's abundance, not enjoyed by another —

children.text: janmāntare 'pi mama saiva gatir yathā syāt
children.translated_text: [praying] that she alone may be my refuge in another birth also.

children.text: adya api tām avahitāṃ manasa ācalena
janma-antare 'pi mama sa aiva gatir yathā syāt

children.translated_text: Even now, [I think of her] with cheeks kissed by swarms of bees
wandering about, attracted by the fragrance of the lotus of her face —
the tinkling of the bracelets on her sprout-like hands playfully waving
utterly bewilders my mind.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ nakhapadaṃ stanamaṇḍale yad dattaṃ
children.translated_text: Even now I remember the nail-mark that was placed upon the circle of her breast
by me, intoxicated by drinking the wine of her face —
with many goosebumps bristling all around,
it keeps watch, guards, and gazes [at her] — I remember.

children.text: adya api tāṃ nakha-padaṃ stana-maṇḍale yad dattaṃ

children.translated_text: Even now I remember: [when she,] face turned away in anger, wished to go
and gave no spoken word in reply — when I
kissed [her], she wept profusely; I fell at [her] feet [saying:]

children.text: dāsas tava priyatame bhaja maṃ smarāmi
children.translated_text: 'I am your slave, dearest! Accept me!' — I remember.

children.text: na uktaṃ vacaḥ pratidadāti yada aiva vaktram
dāsas tava priyatame bhaja maṃ smarāmi
adyāpi dhavati manaḥ kim ahaṃ karomi
children.translated_text: Even now my mind races — what can I do?
In the pleasure-chamber with her friends, in beautiful surroundings,
amidst the varied dances of playful embraces of a beloved's limbs —
'Let my time pass in such delightful play!' — [thus I wish].

children.text: adya api dhavati manaḥ kim ahaṃ karomi
adyāpi tāṃ jagati varṇayituṃ na kaś cic
children.translated_text: Even now, no one in the world is able
to describe her, my wife, whose equal has never been seen;

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ tayor sadṛśayor khalu yena rūpaṃ
children.translated_text: if one were indeed to see the form of two [women] equal [to her],

children.text: śakto bhaved yadi saiva naro na cānyaḥ
children.translated_text: that person alone could [describe her], and no other.

children.text: adya api tāṃ jagati varṇayituṃ na kaś cic
dṛṣṭaṃ tayor sadṛśayor khalu yena rūpaṃ
śakto bhaved yadi sa eva naro na ca anyaḥ
adyāpi tāṃ na khalu vedmi kim īśapatnī
children.translated_text: Even now, I truly do not know whether she is the wife of <s>Īśa</s> (Śiva)
fallen under a curse, or the dark <s>Lakṣmī</s> of the lord of gods,
or whether she was created by the Creator himself for the delusion of the world,
or from the desire to behold a jewel among women.

children.text: adya api tāṃ na khalu vedmi kim īśa-patnī
dhātra aiva kiṃ nu jagataḥ parimohanāya

children.translated_text: Even now [I see] the collyrium of her eyes, her radiant face,
her tranquil pair of ears — for the sake of jest [she said:]
'I see upon your own [body], from [the pressing of my] fresh young breasts,

children.text: kṣīṇāṃ vapur yadi vinaśyati no na doṣaḥ
children.translated_text: your body is wasted — if it perishes, that is no fault [of mine].'

children.text: kṣīṇāṃ vapur yadi vinaśyati no na doṣaḥ

children.translated_text: Even now, [her] face, fair as the spotless autumn moon —

children.text: ceto muner api haret kim utāsmadīyam
children.translated_text: it would steal the mind even of a sage, how much more mine!

children.text: vaktraṃ sudhāmayam ahaṃ yadi tat prapadye
children.translated_text: If I were to reach that nectarean face,

children.text: cumban pibāmy avirataṃ vyadhate mano me
children.translated_text: kissing [it], I would drink [it] ceaselessly — [thus] my mind is pierced.

children.text: ceto muner api haret kim uta asmadīyam
vaktraṃ sudhā-mayam ahaṃ yadi tat prapadye
cumban pibāmy avirataṃ vyadhate mano me

children.translated_text: Even now, [her body] fragrant with the sweet scent of lotus pollen,
that water of love, bringing about the downfall of the Makara-bannered one (<s>Kāma</s>) —
if I should again attain that sole holy place of love-making,
I would surely give up my life-breaths for the sake of attaining it.
Even now, alas, in this world filled with hundreds of thousands of beautiful women,
each endowed with surpassing excellent qualities,

children.text: anyābhir apy upamituṃ na mayā ca śakyaṃ
children.translated_text: I am unable to compare her with any other—

children.text: rūpaṃ tadīyam iti me hṛdaye vitarkaḥ
children.translated_text: 'her beauty is incomparable'—such is the reflection in my heart.

children.text: anyābhir apy upamituṃ na mayā ca śakyaṃ
rūpaṃ tadīyam iti me hṛdaye vitarkaḥ

children.translated_text: Even now she, the river of my mind, ever remains—
vast in nature, with waves of horripilation playing upon her;
with the radiance of <s>kadamba</s> filaments, gazing at wounded me,
she speaks of my bodily exhaustion—my beloved royal swan.

children.text: adya api sā mama manas-taṭinī sadā āste

children.translated_text: Even now she, with limbs beautiful in fresh youth,
her slender body trembling with waves of horripilation,
from the deep mud of separation stirring the essence of my heart,
moves ever so slightly—my beloved royal swan.
Even now I think of her, that daughter of King <s>Śekhara</s>,
her eyes rolling languidly with the intoxication of full youth,
a maiden surpassing <s>Gandharva</s>, <s>Yakṣa</s>, <s>Sura</s>, <s>Kiṃnara</s>, and <s>Nāga</s> maidens—
alas, I think of her as though fallen from heaven.
Even now I remember her, with her slender waist like a sacrificial altar,
with a pair of high, well-rounded breast-vessels filled with nectar,
her limbs adorned with various wonderful ornamental designs—

children.text: suptotthitāṃ niśi divā na hi vismarāmi
children.translated_text: risen from sleep, night or day, I do not forget her.

children.text: supta-utthitāṃ niśi divā na hi vismarāmi

children.translated_text: Even now I remember her, with languid limbs radiant as gold,
bashful yet eager, moving as though overcome [by modesty],
bewildered with desire born from the embrace of limb with limb and kissing—
I remember that young woman as though she were the elixir of life.
Even now I recall that weaponless battle of love-sport,
hands left empty from the binding, releasing, falling, and rising [of embraces],
sprinkled with blood from the biting of lips and scratching of nails—
I remember the beautiful fierceness of her love-making.
Even now I, sustained by the enjoyment of love-making with my excellent bride,
live; by no other means, not even for a moment without her.

children.text: tad bhrātaro maraṇam eva hi duḥkha
children.translated_text: Therefore, brothers, death alone for the cessation of suffering—
I beseech you: cut swiftly!

children.text: tad bhrātaro maraṇam eva hi duḥkha

children.translated_text: Even now <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) does not abandon the <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison;
the tortoise indeed bears the earth upon its back;
the ocean bears the unbearable submarine fire (<s>vaḍavāgni</s>)—
the virtuous protect what they have accepted.

children.text: adya api na ujjhati haraḥ kila kāla-kūṭaṃ
